The api died because the disk filled up: the `report-export` job wrote 40 CSV parts of 512 MB each (about 20 GB) into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` between 03:05:00 and 03:12:48, on the same volume Postgres uses.

The disk warning hit 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 the db failed with `could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device`, the api aborted its transaction and shut down its worker pool, and at 03:14:06 it exited with status 1.

From 03:16:00 the proxy logged `upstream api refused connection` every two minutes through 05:28:00, and the log ends at 05:29:57 with no successful api request after the crash. So the api never recovered inside this log, even with `restart: unless-stopped`. Web and proxy kept serving 200s throughout. The `cache: slow command` warnings run every five minutes from the first line of the log, so they are background noise, not part of this.

To recover, free space by deleting or moving the `part-*.csv` files in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, then confirm Postgres is healthy and restart the api. To stop a repeat, move the exports to a different volume than the database or cap the job's output. The job's code isn't in this repo, so I couldn't see why it wrote that much.

The log's timestamps are all 2026-03-09, not last night, so check this is the right file for the outage you mean.
